- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate, especially in early forecast periods — reduce early forecast peaks.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates — increase early forecast values, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00) by overshooting 2–3x in 30d forecast — cap or dampen extreme early peaks.
- After a sharp price spike (true > 10x history mean), model often fails to correct — add a “mean reversion” buffer: if true > 15x recent mean, reduce forecast by 20–40% in next 5–7 days.
- Sentiment + price history shows strong correlation: if sentiment is rising and price is trending up, model should not lag — adjust forecast to match sentiment momentum.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) — increase forecast by 10–20% in early horizon if sentiment is “flat” or “slightly positive”.
- For 30d forecasts, model often fails to capture “late-stage” true price surges — if sentiment is positive and true outcome exceeds 3x recent mean, apply “late-stage multiplier” (e.g., +1.5x) to final 5–7 days.
